status_as_of_cutoff: approved-permitted / pre-construction: Missouri DED and Google confirm a planned New Florence/Montgomery County data center investment. The Montgomery County project page now publishes Project Spade materials, and current project materials describe two initial data-center buildings with construction anticipated in late 2026. County-linked/current secondary records describe the site as permitted-by-right after Montgomery County administrative review, with site-plan, stormwater/grading, water/wastewater, and Ameren/MISO documentation present; an MDNR land-disturbance stormwater permit is reported for Project Lumberjack, part of Project Spade. No direct county building permit, certificate of occupancy, energization, commissioning, or operating/service record was located.

actions.result_status: Current county-linked records and public reporting describe a Data Center Administrative Review for Project Spade in a Commercial Zoned District: the project was treated as a permitted-by-right data center use, with site plan, grading/stormwater, MDNR well/water documentation, wastewater disposal, electric provider agreement, Ameren/MISO documentation, and utility relocation outlines present. Several operational-impact details were still reported as blank or unresolved.
actions.access_caveat: The county page was discoverable via search and lists Project Spade Site Plan/FAQ materials, but the page/PDF could not be directly opened during this refresh from the local shell or browser tool; detailed review facts are corroborated by an accessible 2025 public records write-up and industry trackers rather than direct county-document text.
actions.evidence_note: Moves local-process evidence above announcement-only, but does not prove vertical construction, building permit issuance, CO, energization, or operation.

actions.action_type: land disturbance / stormwater operating permit reported
actions.result_status: Public records reporting identifies Missouri State Operating Permit MORA29107 issued to Spade Property Owner LLC for Project Lumberjack, described as part of Project Spade, at 580 Tree Farm Road, New Florence, covering 23.04 acres of land disturbance activity and valid until 2027-02-07.
actions.access_caveat: Permit details were located through an accessible public-records write-up; MDNR's public data-center page confirms land-disturbance permit requirements for one or more disturbed acres, but the specific permit record was not directly retrievable from MDNR search during this refresh.
actions.evidence_note: Supports site-work-preparation evidence, not data-center building construction or operation.

actions.government_body: Missouri Department of Economic Development / Google
actions.result_status: The state announced Google's $15 billion Missouri infrastructure investment and identified a new data center in Montgomery County/New Florence, along with energy and community commitments. The release does not identify a parcel, permit, or local vote.
actions.access_caveat: State economic-development announcement is not local zoning, building, environmental, or utility approval.
actions.evidence_note: Official state/company announcement; capacity for this project remains undisclosed.

actions.result_status: The project website identifies a closed-loop, non-evaporative, air-cooled Google data-center campus in Montgomery County, lists two initial data-center buildings plus support buildings, 300 local jobs, and construction anticipated in late 2026.
actions.access_caveat: Partner/economic-development website, not a county permit or construction record; the target date is not independently verified.
actions.evidence_note: Tier-4 project-site context kept separate from official action.

actions.result_status: Google's current location material lists New Florence, Missouri as in development without a project-specific construction or service date.
actions.access_caveat: Company page; location listing does not establish local approval or operation.

actions.result_status: The project site now links a Water Risk Assessment Summary for the Cambrian-Ordovician Aquifer, completed in Q1 2026. It reports low chronic depletion risk and no curtailment events, but high current and future water-scarcity risk ratios for the aquifer and high risk of more intense precipitation events in the region.
actions.access_caveat: Project-posted technical memo; not a regulatory approval and not an operating water-use report.
actions.evidence_note: Current project environmental context; does not establish operating withdrawal volumes.

capacity_notes.value: Project-specific IT/electric capacity remains officially undisclosed. Google says it has contracted for more than 1 GW of new generation capacity in Missouri and is supporting more than 500 MW of additional capacity with Ameren, but those figures are broader Missouri energy commitments, not stated Project Spade load.
Data Center Dynamics, citing industry/project context, reports Project Spade as targeting 1.2 GW on a 934-acre plot developed by Related Digital.
